text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A U.S. fund has bought Bulgarian Brady bonds worth one billion dollars, said Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov who is in Washington for the International Monetary Fund/World bank annual meeting.
Filipov did nod identify the fund.
-- Bulgarian notes of one, two, five and 10 levs issued in 1962 and 1974 will be a legal tender by the end of this year, the central bank said.

-- Bulgaria may fail to get a $25 million loan for grain imports under the U.S. GSM 102 programme because the Bulgarian bank that is expected to provide the loan guarantee, Bulbank, considers the loan unfavourable, Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry officials said.

-- Bulgaria's tourist firm Balkan Holidays plans to settle an outstanding $4.5 million debt to three Bulgarian Black Sea resorts with company shares, Bulgaria's Tourism Committee chairman Vassil Velev said.

-- Bulgaria's Finance Ministry is in talks with United Bulgarian Bank and Bulgarian Post Bank to meet pending payments on government securities sold to Bulgarians by banks put under special supervision by the central bank last week due to a danger of insolvency.
-- Prices of government-monitored basic goods rose by 11.8 percent in the second half of September, National Statistics Institute officials said.
-- Bulgaria's Pleven-based oil refinery Plama will resume production on October 15 which was suspended in March due to a lack of funds for crude oil imports, Plama's owner Euroenergy Holding said.

-- Bulgaria's Bulbank is in talks for buying a majority stake in the state-owned Economic Bank which was put under special supervision by the BNB last week due to a danger of insolvency, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's Supreme Court rejected an appeal by First Private Bank (FPB) against the central bank's decision of May 17 to put the FPB under special supervision and to dismiss its board of directors.

-- Bulgaria's Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov and Trade Minister Atanas Paparizov called for urgent wheat imports to alleviate a grain shortage in talks with the ambassadors of European Union member countries to Sofia.
